title: Discovery Call — Northwind Traders
overview: Northwind's 120 sales reps log call notes inconsistently, so pipeline reviews rely on gut feeling.
Reps spend about 5 hours a week on notes and CRM updates, roughly 600 hours across the team.
They evaluated Gong last year but found it too expensive and too heavy for reps.
Requirements: Salesforce integration, EU data residency, SOC 2 Type II, a signed DPA and Okta SSO.
Next step is a 30-day pilot with 20 reps; budget is approved for Q1 and the CRO makes the final call.

chapters.title: Budget & decision process
chapters.summary: Budget is approved for Q1 on the Business plan; the CRO decides after a pilot.

chapters.title: Pilot plan & next steps
chapters.summary: A 30-day pilot with 20 reps. Success means 90% of calls logged and at least 2 hours saved per rep each week.

action_items.text: Send the security package and completed security questionnaire

Review the security documents and DPA

comments.body: These success criteria are great. Let's copy them into the mutual action plan word for word.

transcript: Daniel Okafor: Hi Laura, hi Tom, thanks for making the time. I've got Jordan from our product team with me today. The plan is to understand how your sales team works today, then show you a few things, and agree on next steps if it makes sense.
Laura Bennett: Sounds good. Just for context, I run sales operations at Northwind. Tom leads IT and he'll have the security questions.
Daniel Okafor: Perfect. So to start, can you walk us through how your reps handle call notes today?

Laura Bennett: Honestly, it's inconsistent. We have about a hundred and twenty reps across three regions. Some take great notes, most type a couple of lines into Salesforce after the call, and some don't log anything at all.
Laura Bennett: The result is that our pipeline reviews are based on gut feeling. When a deal slips, nobody can tell me what the customer actually said about budget or timing.
Jordan Rivera: That's a really common pattern. How much time do you think reps spend on notes and CRM updates per week?
Laura Bennett: We surveyed them last quarter. The average was about five hours a week. For a team of a hundred and twenty, that's a lot of selling time.
Daniel Okafor: That's six hundred hours a week across the team. If we could give back even half of that, it pays for itself many times over.
Laura Bennett: That's the business case I need to make to our CFO, so I like that framing.
Daniel Okafor: Have you looked at other tools?
Laura Bennett: We evaluated Gong last year. It's powerful, but it was too expensive for the full team, and the reps found it heavy. We need something they'll actually use without training.

Jordan Rivera: That's exactly where we focus. Notes are generated automatically and pushed to Salesforce, so the rep doesn't have to change their workflow. They just review the summary and the action items.

Tom Fischer: Can I jump in with the IT side? The Salesforce integration is a must have, but I need to understand how data flows. Where are recordings stored, and do you support data residency in the EU? About forty of our reps are in Germany.
Jordan Rivera: Recordings and transcripts are encrypted at rest. We have an EU data region in Frankfurt, and workspaces can be pinned to it so data never leaves the EU.
Tom Fischer: Good. What about compliance? We'll need SOC 2 Type Two and a signed DPA.
Daniel Okafor: We have SOC 2 Type Two, renewed in August, and a standard DPA. I'll send the security package over today, including our completed security questionnaire.
Tom Fischer: And single sign-on? We use Okta for everything.
Jordan Rivera: SAML single sign-on with Okta is shipping this quarter. In fact, your requirement is one of the reasons we prioritized it.
Tom Fischer: Okay. If SSO isn't live, a pilot is still fine, but the full rollout would depend on it.
Laura Bennett: Let's talk about budget and timing. We have budget approved for a tool like this starting in Q1. What would pricing look like for a hundred and twenty seats?

Daniel Okafor: For your size, the Business plan makes the most sense. It includes the Salesforce integration, unlimited transcription, and the EU data region. I'll put together a proposal with volume pricing for a hundred and twenty seats.
Laura Bennett: Great. On the decision process, I'm the business owner, Tom signs off on security, and our CRO has the final say. She'll want to see results from a pilot first.
Jordan Rivera: What would a successful pilot look like for you?
Laura Bennett: Twenty reps for thirty days. If we see CRM notes logged for at least ninety percent of calls, and reps tell us they save at least two hours a week, that's a win.
Daniel Okafor: Those are clear criteria. Let's set up the pilot for twenty reps starting the first week of next month. I'll send a mutual action plan with the dates.
Tom Fischer: Before the pilot starts I'll need a technical call with your team to review the Salesforce permissions and the SSO setup.
Daniel Okafor: Of course. Jordan, could you join that technical call with Tom next week, along with one of our engineers?
Jordan Rivera: Yes, I'll bring Marcus, he's leading the SSO work.
Laura Bennett: Perfect. Then I'll pick the twenty pilot reps, a mix of new and senior people across the three regions.

Daniel Okafor: Great. To recap, I'll send the security package and the proposal, set up the pilot for twenty reps, and schedule the technical call. Laura picks the pilot group, and Tom reviews the security documents.
Laura Bennett: That works. Thanks both, this was really helpful.
